plans.topic: How the auditory cortex uses spectrotemporal acoustic patterns to help listeners distinguish speech from music, using a continuous film soundtrack as the research context.
plans.core_claim: The study reports that temporal acoustic patterns carry information useful for speech judgments while spectral patterns carry information useful for music judgments; it does not establish that these are the brain's only categorization mechanisms.
plans.title: How the Brain Separates Speech and Music
plans.hook: How does your brain separate speech from music?
plans.description: Medical Xpress (19 November 2026) and MedicalPress (20 November 2026) report on the same Science Advances study. It links speech judgments with rapid temporal changes and music judgments with detailed frequency patterns. The original film soundtrack is research context only; no film audio or footage will be used.
plans.cover_payoff: Use an original violin phrase twice: first with a clear rhythmic contour, then with a contrasting sustained phrase. Explain timing and frequency patterns with readable, non-numeric graphics; do not use Harry Potter soundtrack audio or film footage.

sources.title: The Harry Potter soundtrack helps researchers test how the brain differentiates speech and background music
Cómo distingue el cerebro la voz de la música: el papel del córtex auditivo

plans.narration_script: How does your brain separate speech and music? Medical Xpress says auditory cortex uses acoustic patterns to distinguish them. MedicalPress links speech with timing, music with frequency patterns. Researchers tested listeners with a film soundtrack.

narration_evidence.quote: the brain's auditory cortex differentiates between speech and music using patterns that describe how acoustic energy changes over time and across frequencies.
Habla: los juicios dependían sobre todo de los cambios rápidos del sonido a lo largo del tiempo. Música: los juicios dependían sobre todo de los patrones detallados entre frecuencias.
11 epilepsy patients with clinically implanted electrodes listened to nearly eight minutes of the French-dubbed soundtrack of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone."
